definitions.explanation: Fish or other seafood that has been preserved by drying, typically split open and sun-dried or wind-dried. A traditional Japanese food preparation method.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}ごはんに{鯵|あじ}の{干物|ひもの}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I had dried horse mackerel for breakfast.

examples.japanese: {海沿|うみぞ}いの{町|まち}では{店先|みせさき}に{干物|ひもの}が{並|なら}べられ、{潮|しお}の{香|かお}りと{一緒|いっしょ}に{旅行者|りょこうしゃ}を{迎|むか}えてくれる。
examples.english: In the coastal town, dried fish are laid out at storefronts, welcoming travelers along with the scent of the sea.

notes:
STRUCTURE:
{干|ひ} (dry) + {物|もの} (thing). Literally "dried thing."

USAGE:
{干物|ひもの} primarily refers to dried fish, which is a staple of traditional Japanese breakfasts. Common types include {鯵|あじ} (horse mackerel), {鯖|さば} (mackerel), and {鰯|いわし} (sardine). The fish is typically split open ({開|ひら}き), salted, and dried. {干物|ひもの} is often associated with seaside towns and {旅館|りょかん} (Japanese inns). Colloquially, {干物|ひもの}{女|おんな} ("dried fish woman") is slang for a woman who stays home and lives a lazy lifestyle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干物|ひもの}を{焼|や}く: to grill dried fish
- {鯵|あじ}の{干物|ひもの}: dried horse mackerel
- {干物|ひもの}{屋|や}: dried fish shop
- {自家製|じかせい}{干物|ひもの}: homemade dried fish
